When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index **2/10**, calm vs VIX Spike Tier **2/4** MEDIUM, **60%** probability, backwardation and skew active
Price is quiet while options traders pay up for protection. Trust the VIX read for sizing, because options reprice before stocks do, and the Crash Index only confirms damage after it lands.
⚠ These two disagree: Contrarian score **58**, accumulate vs Regime score **41** with **3** risk-off signals aligned
One gauge says buy weakness while the other says defend. Trust the risk-off read for now. The contrarian score is only a partial signal, and dip buying works best once VIX backwardation clears.
Today's tension
Price action is calm while options and cross-asset signals lean toward a top
Bull
The Crash Index sits at only **2** out of **10**, no confluence is active, and the contrarian gauge at **58** says dip buyers are starting to get paid. Dow strength at **+0.2%** over five days shows the index is holding.
Bear
VIX backwardation and skew are both active, **20** of **43** tracked pairs lean bearish against **7** bullish, and the Nasdaq 100 lags at **-3.7%** over five days. Options traders are paying for protection that price has not yet required.
The tell: VIX backwardation fading back to normal term structure would clear the bear case. A Crash Index move above **2** with backwardation still on would confirm it.
AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

You're in a market that looks calm and is being priced as fragile. The Crash Index reads 2 out of 10, yet the regime score of 41 sits in transition with 3 risk-off signals lined up. The divergence composite reads TOPPING, with 62.8% of pairs diverging.

That shapes positioning. The macro regime is INFLATIONARY at only 45% confidence, so conviction is thin everywhere. The contrarian score of 58 says accumulate on a partial signal, and the VIX Spike tier of 2 out of 4 says protection is getting bid. Keep gross exposure near neutral, build any new longs in small pieces, and keep hedges on while backwardation lasts. Nasdaq 100 weakness at -3.7% over five days is the place to look first if the top is forming.

The main risk is a vol expansion that arrives before the Crash Index reacts. The reading that flips the stance is VIX backwardation going away while the regime score climbs back above 41. That would turn the contrarian 58 into a real buy signal.

Macro Regime — where are we structurally
AI read · macro regime

The macro regime reads INFLATIONARY at 45% confidence. That is under half, so treat it as a lean and size accordingly.

An inflationary regime favors real assets and pricing power over long-duration growth. The Nasdaq 100 lag at -3.7% over five days fits that.

The broken SPY to TLT link, which went from +0.69 to -0.39, also fits: bonds are no longer hedging stocks the way they usually do. Hold less duration, favor cash flow over distant earnings, and keep position size modest until confidence moves clearly above 45%.

Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence means two things that normally move together have started moving apart. Correlation drift is the measure of that: how much the link between two series has changed over recent weeks. The composite zone reads TOPPING, with 62.8% of the 43 pairs diverging, 20 leaning bearish and 7 bullish. The mother jaws score is 100.

Six pairs sit at 80 and all read DEEP DIVERG. The QQQ to SPY link drifted from +0.90 to -0.12, so the Nasdaq 100 no longer moves with the S&P 500. Regional banks against the financial sector fell from +0.29 to -0.72. SPY against TLT went from +0.69 to -0.39, and the 10-year minus 2-year yield spread flipped from -0.38 to +0.40. Relationships that held for months are breaking at once, and that pattern tends to show up near turning points. It does not give a date.

HYG weakness is the most likely one to turn this into a real defensive call.

Cross-Region Surveillance
Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

The 24/7 picture is split. In Asia, the Hang Seng is flat at -0.1% over five days while the KOSPI sits at -14.5%, a sharp single-market break that points to local stress and not a region-wide sell-off.

Europe is steady, with Switzerland at +4.4% and the Euro Stoxx 50 at +0.5%, which shows defensives holding up. In the US, the Dow at +0.2% holds while the Nasdaq 100 trails at -3.7%.

Crypto is quiet, with Solana at +0.9% and Ether at -0.5%. The lead-lag read for the US session is that growth is the weak spot and defensives are the safe place.

Watch the Nasdaq 100 at the open, and check whether the KOSPI weakness spreads to other tech-heavy markets.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 2/10 · WATCH — 1-2 signals, monitoring
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

The Crash Index at 2 out of 10 and the VIX Spike Detector at tier 2 of 4 (MEDIUM, 60% probability) describe the same market from two angles. The Crash Index measures damage in price. It sees almost none. The VIX detector measures what options traders expect, and it sees stress ahead: skew is active, so downside puts cost more than upside calls, and backwardation is active, so near-term fear is priced above longer-dated fear.

That combination is coherent. Price is calm because nothing has broken yet, and options are bid because traders expect something might. The adaptive trigger is off, so the signal is not yet at its strongest. Treat the options read as the early warning. A Crash Index that climbs above 2 while backwardation stays on would mean price is finally catching up.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 2/10, so the tape is calm and there is no crash setup.

How to read
Each row = an independent signal Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY. The structural (DXY, SKEW, MOVE) signal a regime change over 30-90 days. The stress (HYG/IEF, VIX3M/VIX, STLFSI4) ring at 5-30 days. The triggers (SPY -2% in 5d, VIX +30% in 3d) are short-term breakouts. For a tactical decision: 3+ signals simultaneously aligned = real probability of stress, never on isolated signal (framework rule).

How to read
Aggregation of all panel signals across the 4 cross-asset buckets. RISK-ON = risk appetite (cyclical, equity, EM). RISK-OFF = flight to defensives (TLT, gold, JPY). STRESS = liquidity tension (HYG, MOVE, STLFSI). TOPPING = end-of-cycle signals (concentration, breadth narrowing, defensives leading). Doctrine: a single signal = noise. 3+ aligned in one bucket = real confirmed regime.

How to read
Heat ranking: composite of RS (relative strength vs SPY), Momentum (price action 20-60d), Breadth (% stocks above SMA), Options flow, and Attention. Use top-5 as rotation focus.

Competitor themes: token frequency × recency across top finance Substacks — useful narrative context, not a trading signal.
Best R/R: only entries with an active screener leg (PULLBACK / BOTTOM / SMART_MONEY_SURGE etc.). EV% = probabilistic edge per trade. Cross-check with weekly chart before sizing.

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
